name: The Lakefire Collapse — Okonkwo-Paz Night, 2211
creator: Lakefire Cultural Consortium (independent)
description: The seventh annual Lakefire Great Lakes Multicultural Food & Synthesis Festival ended catastrophically on August 14th, 2211, when a structural failure in the repurposed Pier 7 warehouse complex sent three elevated stage platforms into Lake Michigan, killing 41 attendees and injuring over 300. The night had been dubbed 'Okonkwo-Paz Night' by festivalgoers after headlining performers Adaeze Okonkwo-Paz and her ensemble were scheduled to close the festival with a landmark neural-acoustic set — a performance that never happened. The collapse exposed years of ignored infrastructure safety reports that the Consortium had buried to secure cheaper venue permits from a HelixCorp subsidiary.
medium: physical event / neural feed broadcast / subsequent documentary archive
cultural_impact: The disaster permanently fractured public trust in independently organized Tier 1-2 cultural events and ignited the Venue Safety Accords of 2212, which critics argued were designed primarily to price out underground festivals rather than improve safety. 'Okonkwo-Paz Night' became shorthand in the Gray Zone communities for the way institutions allow infrastructure to fail the poor until bodies make the news.
controversy: HelixCorp's subsidiary Verdant Venue Solutions was implicated in suppressing the structural assessment reports but faced no criminal prosecution; three mid-level Consortium organizers were convicted instead. Adaeze Okonkwo-Paz's public accusation of HelixCorp during her grief statement was scrubbed from official neural feed archives within 48 hours, though pirate copies circulate widely in the Gray Zone.
story_hooks: A journalist discovers a complete unedited copy of Adaeze Okonkwo-Paz's scrubbed grief statement and must decide whether publishing it is worth the corporate retaliation that will follow.
One of the survivors, now a decade older, learns that the engineer who first filed the suppressed safety report is living under a new identity in the Gray Zone — and wants to talk.

A young organizer planning a new the Gray Zone festival is approached by someone claiming to be from Verdant Venue Solutions, offering suspiciously generous venue terms — the same deal that preceded the collapse.
